page.overview:
Who is Ahr?

Ahr was a human male Moff and governor of the Esuain sector in the Mid Rim who commanded a Venator-class Star Destroyer in the Galactic Empire's navy. Along with the Sith Lord Darth Vader, he was assigned to neutralize a threat on Namzor around 2 BBY. However, during the Namzor counter-insurgency, Vader committed insubordination, resulting in Ahr contacting Emperor Palpatine, who ordered Vader to abide by all the governor's directives.

Ahr and Vader went on to liquidate threats on Ahn Krantarium and Phelzepham, both of which resulted in successes. After dealing with the three problems, the Moff wanted Vader to kill a creature as a test, but the Sith Lord had other plans. After seeing the creature from his starship, Vader turned around and made it rupture the bridge, grasping and killing Ahr in space.

Ahr served as the Moff and governor of in the Mid Rim in the Galactic Empire as well as the commanding officer of a Venator-class Star Destroyer in the Imperial Navy. Around 2 BBY, as part of a pacification operation, he was sent to deal with insurgents on the Mid Rim astronomical object Namzor with the Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Vader. However, the insurgents had set up their base over a coaxium hypermatter deposit. Ahr, who had been instructed to obtain the coaxium, ordered all starfighters to return to the Star Destroyer to avoid damaging the coaxium. The Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter withdrew, but Vader, in his starship, did not. Despite the Moff ordering the Sith Lord to pull back, Vader continued attacking the base until he destroyed both the insurgents and the coaxium deposit.

A very displeased Ahr contacted Emperor Palpatine via hologram to report Vader's failure to follow orders, his arriving unannounced, and his destruction of the valuable coaxium. However, Vader disagreed, stating that he had destroyed the insurgents so that they could not escape. Palpatine questioned Vader about his awareness of the governor's orders and then commanded Vader to follow all of Ahr's orders as if they were from Palpatine himself until he had learned his lesson. Vader was angry about the outcome, seeing himself as nothing more than a slave to others.
